fix(mobile): match board header icons to the Workers filter colour on iOS

Code changes: +10 -3\
Tests: +0 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

On iOS, the Settings, Pull Requests and Notifications icons in the board header now use the theme's text colour, the same as the Workers filter icon across from them.

## Why

The filter icon followed the theme (cream in the screenshot), but the three icons on the right were plain white. iOS draws bar items without the shared glass background in the system label colour and ignores the bar's tint, so those three never picked up the theme.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: filter icon cream, gear, PR and bell icons white](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/66bc5c5788b37af3079c69dbadae2529/raw/2cf388d941cc4a0681910f922e7f073beabf7d3e/before.jpg) | ![After: filter, gear, PR and bell icons all cream](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ronishrohan/66bc5c5788b37af3079c69dbadae2529/raw/2cf388d941cc4a0681910f922e7f073beabf7d3e/after.png) |

## How

`BoardHeaderItems` reads the theme and passes `tintColor={t.textPrimary}` to the three bar buttons on iOS. That is the colour `worker-filter-menu.ios.tsx` already uses for the filter glyph. The unread badge keeps its own colour. Android is unchanged: its top app bar already tints these buttons and the filter the same way. The "+" create action keeps the accent tint, since it is an action rather than a bare glyph.

## Testing

- Tested manually on an iPhone 16 with a Debug build of this branch: the gear, PR and bell icons now match the filter icon (After screenshot).
- Local checks not run; GitHub Actions handles validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch)
- [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable
- [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene
- [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording
- [ ] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense
- [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.)

Keep the storage endpoint Azure adds to the database subnet

## Summary
- **Drift found:** `terraform plan` against the live environment showed an in-place change to the database subnet, removing a `Microsoft.Storage` service endpoint. Azure adds that endpoint itself when it creates the PostgreSQL Flexible Server, which uses it for backups and logs. The next `terraform apply` would have stripped it.
- **Fix:** the `network` module takes optional `service_endpoints` per subnet, and the `db` subnet declares `["Microsoft.Storage"]`, so the configuration matches what Azure needs.

## How to test
```bash
git fetch && git checkout fix/96-db-subnet-storage-endpoint
cd terraform
terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
terraform plan    # No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.
```
Before this change the same plan reported `0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy` on `module.network.azurerm_subnet.this["db"]`. Checkov: 37 passed, 0 failed.

Follow-up to #102, part of #94.

diff --git a/terraform/main.tf b/terraform/main.tf
index 3f4cd5f..47ec093 100644
--- a/terraform/main.tf
+++ b/terraform/main.tf
@@ -34,6 +34,8 @@ module "network" {
     db = {
       address_prefix = local.subnet_prefixes.db
       delegation     = "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers"
+      # Azure adds this endpoint when it creates the server, for backups and logs. Declaring it keeps apply from removing it.
+      service_endpoints = ["Microsoft.Storage"]
       inbound_rules = {
         postgres-from-app = { priority = 100, port = "5432", source = local.subnet_prefixes.app }
         within-subnet     = { priority = 110, port = "*", source = local.subnet_prefixes.db }

index 3501a32..b7bcb69 100644

   virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.this.name
   address_prefixes     = [each.value.address_prefix]
+  service_endpoints    = each.value.service_endpoints

fix(mobile): point Free and failed-payment plans to the desktop Code changes: +31 -12\ Tests: +14 -3\ Others: +0 -0 ## What Mobile now tells a signed-in user without a paid plan (and one whose payment failed) where plans are managed: "Plans are managed in Orchestrator on your desktop." It also stops New task from showing setup hints that Free can't act on. - **New task → Cloud on Free:** shows only the plan message, now ending with the desktop line, plus **See plan**. The "create a cloud project" and "connect a coding agent" hints are gone. Send stays disabled, so Free still can't start a cloud session from the phone. - **Plan sheet** (See plan, or any plan refusal): the desktop line under the plan rows. - **Settings → Orchestrator Cloud:** the desktop line as the Plan footer on Free, and on a paid plan whose payment failed. ## Why On Free, mobile was a dead end. New task pointed to New cloud project and Settings → Orchestrator Cloud's coding agents, but Free hides both. The plan sheet and "Payment failed" gave no next step. Plans are bought on the desktop (Settings → Upgrade), so the phone should say so. ## Before / After | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | | | | The After screenshots were taken before the wording changed from "on your computer" to "on your desktop" (e0ec6e33cb). That commit only changes the text. Captured on an iOS 26.5 simulator (Debug build) against a local fake Cloud control plane with fictional data. Before is from `main`; this PR doesn't touch those screens' code paths otherwise. ## How - `PLAN_DESKTOP_NOTE` in `lib/cloud/plan.ts` is the single string, used by the Free block, the plan sheet and both Settings footers. - `planBlocksCloudSetup()` is true only for the Free block (`reason: "plan"`). New task then skips the cloud-project hint and `spawnNotices`. Skipping the catalog error alone would have surfaced its "no agent supports Chat" notice instead. A spent usage window still shows the setup hints, because those users can act on them. - The Settings footer uses `SettingsSection`'s always-mounted footer slot, so it doesn't rebuild the section (#7906). - App Store: the line names where plans are managed, with no link, price, or upgrade button. That keeps the phone the desktop companion that `plan.ts` describes. A unit test pins the copy to no URL, `$`, "upgrade", "buy" or "subscribe". ## Testing - `npx vitest run` in `packages/mobile`: 440 files, 4233 tests pass (new cases for the Free block copy, `planBlocksCloudSetup` and the note). - `npm run typecheck` in `packages/mobile`: passes. - Manually on the simulator: Free (New task, plan sheet, Settings → Cloud) and Starter with `past_due`, as in the table. ## Checklist - [x] Branched from `main` (or continuing an existing PR branch) - [x] One focused change; links the related issue when applicable - [x] Follows [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/AGENTS.md) conventions and PR hygiene - [x] Before / After filled in; UI changes include screenshots or a recording - [x] Tests added/updated for user-visible behavior where it makes sense - [ ] Relevant CI checks pass for the area touched (`go`, frontend, etc.) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Cloud plan views explain that plans are managed in Orchestrator on desktop. * **Changes** * Cloud setup guidance and related notices are hidden when a plan blocks setup. * Free-plan messages include desktop plan-management guidance. * Paid-plan views show the guidance when the plan status indicates a problem; otherwise, they show no footer note.

fix: keep the inbox and a channel agreeing on what was read

## What

Reading a message in its channel now clears it in the inbox, and choosing a thread reply in the inbox marks only that thread read.

- `messenger.svelte`: when the channel reports a read, the inbox marks its own entries in that conversation or thread read. Nothing is reported while an inbox entry is still being revealed.
- `channel.svelte`: the channel reports no read while a thread covers it in the focus layout.
- `messenger-inbox-state.svelte.ts`: `showReadThrough` updates the entries in place.

## Why

A mention read in its channel stayed unread in the inbox, and the inbox count stayed up, because a read only reread the channel list.

Choosing a thread reply in the inbox showed only the thread, yet the hidden channel behind it was marked read through its latest message. A mention in that channel that the reader never saw stopped counting.

The inbox is updated in place because the relay lists a thread reply only while it is unread. Asking again would drop the row the reader just chose.

## Verification

- `tools/verify --ui messenger`: `environment-declarations`, `verification-plan`, `web` and `web-tests` passed. `ui` reported 201 passed and 8 failed during a 30 minute run on a machine with a load average near 180.
- `./scripts/ui.sh tests/ui/messenger/messenger-mobile-ux.spec.ts tests/ui/messenger/messenger-thread-sheet.spec.ts`: 44 passed. These files hold the 7 tests that timed out above.
- The eighth failure, `messenger-edit-mentions-fixture.spec.ts:69`, also fails on `origin/main`: 9 of 16 repeats failed at `3109acf7f` with `--repeat-each=16`.
- `messenger-inbox-fixture.spec.ts`: 26 passed. The new test `a mention read in its channel stops counting as unread in the inbox` failed before the change with the inbox count still at 2.
- `make check` was not run on this branch. The local relay build fails with a permission error, so the relay groups could not run here.

fix(web): show the sidebar matter meta line at full contrast

Each sidebar matter row's meta line (client and last activity) had `opacity-60` on `text-muted-foreground` at 10px, about 2.5:1 against the sidebar. Its `group-hover/sidebar-menu-button:opacity-100` named a group no ancestor declares (the menu item is `group/menu-item`), so hover never lifted it.

- Drop the opacity cut and its transition; the line keeps `text-muted-foreground`, which clears 4.5:1 on the default sidebar.

fix(db): sincronizar la migración de account lockout y endurecer la lectura de usuarios

## Resumen

La HOME fallaba en local con `User.failedLoginAttempts does not exist` porque la migración `20261118090000_account_lockout` (PR #91) estaba en el repo pero no aplicada en la BD de Neon. `next dev` no aplica migraciones, así que cualquier migración nueva repite el problema.

- **BD**: migración `20261118090000_account_lockout` aplicada con `prisma migrate deploy` (`migrate status` → *Database schema is up to date!*).
- **chore(db)**: `pnpm dev` ahora ejecuta `predev → prisma migrate deploy` (script `db:migrate`), alineando local con CI/Vercel.
- **fix(data)**: `getUsers`/`getUsersByIds` y los `include: { user: true }` de explore/feed usan un `USER_VIEW_SELECT` explícito, así una columna nueva sin migrar ya no convierte las lecturas de boards en `SELECT *` ni tumba la home.
- **test(data)**: regresión que fija que `toUserView` solo proyecta `id`/`username`/`avatarUrl` y descarta `passwordHash`, `sessionVersion`, `failedLoginAttempts`, `lockedUntil` y `twoFactorSecret`.

## Verificación

- `pnpm prisma migrate status` → up to date.
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm lint` ✅
- `pnpm test` ✅ (336 passed, 96 skipped integración sin TEST_DATABASE_URL)
- `GET http://localhost:9002/` → 200 sin el error de Prisma.

## Fuera de alcance

- Otros `findUnique` de auth/settings siguen leyendo la fila completa de `User`; endurecerlos con `select` es una limpieza aparte.
